name: Model 204
tagline: Rocket Software's mainframe inverted-list DBMS, in production since 1972 and still getting releases.
description: Model 204 is a database management system for IBM z/OS mainframes, built by Computer Corporation of America, first deployed in 1972 and now owned and developed by Rocket Software. It predates the relational model: files are inverted-list structures that combine its own bitmap indexes with hashing, B-trees and record lists, applications are written in its SOUL (User Language) 4GL, the Janus add-ons provide web, socket and TLS services, and Model 204 SQL Server gives limited SQL access through explicit file mappings. It copes with very large record counts and heavy transaction rates, which is why agencies such as Services Australia still run core systems on it after a replacement project was scrapped in 2023. Version 8.0 (2026) added TLS 1.3, a built-in SSH server and hardware-accelerated compression: alive, but a system you inherit rather than choose.

pricing.notes: Licensed per mainframe installation through Rocket Software.

scale.notes: Scales vertically on z/OS; known for very large files and high transaction rates on a single system.

strengths: Decades of proven operation for very large government and defense workloads
Bitmap, hash and B-tree indexing gives fast retrieval on huge files
Integrated 4GL (SOUL) plus web and socket serving via Janus
Still actively released by Rocket (8.0 with TLS 1.3 and SSH)
weaknesses: Pre-relational: SQL access is limited and needs explicit mapping
Shrinking pool of SOUL/User Language developers
Migrations off it are notoriously hard and slow
useCases: Maintaining existing government and defense mainframe systems
High-volume record retrieval and update on z/OS
Web-enabling legacy M204 applications through Janus
